absent: Numeric values of shift, segment, alignment, and error tokens.
Initialization, sizing, and growth of bounce pools and atomic pools.
Lookup procedure that maps a physical address to its owning bounce pool.
Search-area probing details and alignment offset computation.
Architecture cache maintenance, encryption toggling, and uncached mapping effects.
Peer to peer mapping state machine and bus address formation.
Contiguous allocator, global pool, and optimal mask selection internals.
Concurrency rules for allocation paths outside slot release.

findings.text: Provides a coherent allocation service that selects among no-mapping, architecture, global pool, atomic pool, bounce pool, and direct contiguous paths based on device coherence and request attributes, then normalizes size, optionally marks pages decrypted, optionally creates an alternate mapping or uncached view, zeroes the visible region, and derives a bus address. Failures release partial state or report an empty result.

Releases a coherent allocation by reversing the path chosen at creation, handling no-mapping cookies, architecture teardown, global pool return, atomic pool return, bounce pool return, or contiguous release, while restoring encryption state and tearing down any alternate mapping. Mismatched global pool returns raise a one-time warning.

Offers a page-oriented coherent allocation pair that honors forced unencrypted mode, uses atomic storage when blocking is unavailable, otherwise prefers bounce backing when configured or direct page acquisition, clears content before use, translates the backing extent to a bus address, and on release restores encryption unless bounce backed or pool owned.

Maps and unmaps scatter collections entry by entry, preserving bus-address entries untouched while translating host entries through a physical mapping helper, recording per-entry lengths, flushing only when host entries were processed on non-coherent devices, and unwinding already mapped leading entries with processor synchronization skipped if a later entry fails.

Translates one physical extent to a bus address with forced-bounce, capability, and small-allocation bounce checks, treating host-encrypted management ranges as shared, rejecting disallowed forced-bounce combinations, delegating to bounce handling when required, otherwise performing device synchronization unless skipped or management range, and reporting overflow through a reserved error token.

Exposes bounce mapping that records a trace event, acquires bounce backing for an origin extent, converts the bounce location to encrypted or shared bus form, validates device capability with cleanup and one-time diagnostic on overflow, synchronizes for non-coherent devices, plus lookup-based release helpers that return success only when the extent belongs to bounce storage.

Supplies contiguous remap helpers that build an array of consecutive page descriptors and map them as one coherent virtual range with caller-supplied protection, and a matching teardown that validates the range belongs to coherent virtual storage before unmapping, warning on misuse.

Determines whether a page or virtual address belongs to atomic coherent storage by scanning candidate pools for a matching chunk, freeing through the owning allocator on hit and reporting ownership as a boolean outcome.

Synchronizes ownership for single extents and scatter collections in both directions, applying processor-side handling and bounce handling in direction-dependent order, with an additional global processor step on the toward-processor path, and skipping all work for management or explicitly coherent requests on unmap.

Slot search starts from a processor-derived area index within the default pool, derives a table bus base honoring shared versus encrypted mode, probes areas cyclically with wraparound, returns the first non-negative probe result, and signals total exhaustion with a negative indicator.

Release recomputes the start slot by compensating alignment and padding, derives slot count from stored allocation length, validates area membership, then under protection rewrites trailing run lengths while invalidating origin and size metadata and extends leading run lengths across contiguous free predecessors before decrementing usage counters.

Direct page acquisition first tries contiguous allocation filtered by optimal mask, coherence, and high-memory policy, discarding unsuitable results, then falls back to buddy allocation with progressively constrained zones, downgrading from default toward narrower device-addressable zones before giving up.

Protection selection preserves caller protection for coherent devices, otherwise chooses write-combined or coherent views per build and request, then applies decrypted or encrypted view according to shared-allocation attributes.

A no-kernel-mapping request without shared allocation bypasses remapping and uses an opaque page cookie with encrypted bus translation after cache preparation, while remap or shared requests that cannot block are diverted to atomic storage when the device is not already served by bounce allocation.

Slot release serializes free-list and usage updates for one area with that area lock held with interrupt state saved, keeping it across run-length merging and local usage decrement, then updates global usage after release.

Bounce state centers on a memory descriptor that selects a default pool and records whether table addresses use shared translation, while each pool records its start, area tally, slabs per area, slot table, and area table, each area records a lock and a used tally, and each slot records list linkage, origin, size, and pad counts.

Streaming helpers treat each scatter entry as carrying a bus address, a transfer length, and a bus-address marker, deriving the processor physical address from the bus address for synchronization and clearing the marker on teardown without touching host mappings.

Coherent creation moves from attribute normalization and size rounding through path selection to page acquisition, optional decryption, optional alternate mapping or uncached conversion with cache preparation, zeroing, and bus translation, with failure edges that unwind remap, restore encryption, and return pages to bounce or contiguous owners, or leak with a diagnostic when re-encryption fails.

Streaming extents move from unmapped to mapped via direct translation or bounce substitution, then alternate between device-owned and processor-owned through direction-specific synchronization, and finally return to unmapped via processor synchronization unless skipped plus bounce teardown, with management and coherent requests bypassing synchronization.

Freeing a virtual address that lacks a coherent virtual area descriptor triggers a warning and leaves the mapping untouched, while failed re-encryption during teardown logs a rate-limited notice and intentionally retains the pages to avoid exposing incorrectly protected memory.

Global usage decrement has two build variants, one forwarding through an indirect static call and one performing no action, so callers cannot assume global accounting occurs. Area membership violation is treated as a fatal programming error before any lock is taken.

Search exhaustion is reported as negative one, allocation and remap failures as NULL, mapping overflow as DMA_MAPPING_ERROR, cleared slot origins as INVALID_PHYS_ADDR, and pool ownership as boolean results.

Request behavior is controlled by attribute flags for no kernel mapping, shared allocation, coherent requirement, management ranges, skip processor synchronization, write combining, and shared coherent views, plus zone and warning modifiers that steer allocator choice.

Slot indexing shifts by IO_TLB_SHIFT and merges within IO_TLB_SEGSIZE with offset handling that avoids crossing segment boundaries, while coherent remaps are tagged with VM_DMA_COHERENT for later validation.
